metasyntax.literal: single-quoted UTF-8 terminal spelling; a double-quoted spelling is used only for a terminal that contains a single quote
metasyntax.choice: terms separated by | inside a parenthesized group; top-level choices are separate alternatives array entries
metasyntax.not_followed_by: !term succeeds without consuming input exactly when term fails at this position

parsing_model: The grammar is a parsing expression grammar. Alternatives are ordered: the alternatives array and each parenthesized choice are tried first to last, and the first alternative that succeeds is the result of that production at that offset. A production is never re-entered at the same offset to try a later alternative after an earlier one succeeded.
Repetition and optional terms are greedy and do not give back input.
Left recursion, direct or indirect, is a grammar defect. A grammar that contains it is rejected when it is loaded.
A frontend grammar is its own tokens and productions merged over those of each imported grammar; a frontend definition replaces an imported definition of the same name.

The source envelope selects library, executable, submission, or script before reading, and reading starts at that root_entrypoints production. The source production is descriptive and is never a parse-success fallback.
terminals: Reading is parser-directed. A terminal is matched only at an offset where a production asks for it; token definitions do not compete globally and carry no precedence. Every token except the frontend's delimiter class, which defines the word boundary, is referenced by at least one production.

Before every terminal the reader consumes skip tokens (whitespace and comments) repeatedly. The Co-Forth parenthesized_comment is not skipped when the terminal being matched is the literal '('; a production that asks for '(' therefore deterministically opens a signature, pattern, or grouping, and '(' anywhere else in a word sequence opens a comment.
A token symbol matches its regular expression, or its named scanner, anchored at the offset. A quoted terminal matches exactly its spelling.

Word boundary: when the last scalar of a matched terminal is XID_Continue or one of - ? !, the next scalar must be end of input, White_Space, a character of the frontend's delimiter token, or the start of a line comment. A contiguous word is therefore never split into several terminals.

Punctuation maximal munch: a quoted terminal whose first scalar is not alphabetic fails when a longer quoted punctuation terminal of the same frontend grammar begins with it and also matches at that offset.

The identifier token never matches a spelling listed in reserved_words of the frontend grammar or of a grammar it imports. A reserved form that begins and then violates its production is a reader error; it cannot fall back to a call or word because its head is not an identifier.
An identifier that is not in Unicode Normalization Form C is a reader error, not an alternative failure.

raw-string, triple-string, coforth-string, and balanced scanners are deterministic single-pass scanners. They never backtrack over content. A string or comment that is opened and not closed is a reader error at its opening offset.
Triple-quoted strings process the same escapes as escaped strings; the closing delimiter is the first unescaped triple quote.
A bare name in type_argument is emitted once as GenericArgument::Name and resolved as Type or Const only from the constructor's declared parameter kind.
errors: F-LEX-INVALID-UTF8: the source is not valid UTF-8; offset is the first invalid byte.
F-LEX-IDENTIFIER-NOT-NFC: offset is the start of the identifier.
F-LEX-UNTERMINATED-STRING, F-LEX-INVALID-ESCAPE, F-LEX-UNBALANCED-COMMENT: offset is the opening delimiter, the backslash, or the opening parenthesis respectively.
F-LEX-SYNTAX: no alternative accepted the source; offset is the farthest byte offset at which any terminal was attempted and failed, after skipped tokens.
normalization: Retain half-open UTF-8 byte spans for every terminal and production node.
Skipped tokens affect line/column projection but emit no syntax or semantic node.
A Co-Forth label token name: normalizes to identifier name followed by the colon terminal.
